title: Jump-start a flat battery with sprung booster clamps in the safe order
instruction: Hook the donor battery on the right up to the flat battery on the left with the red and black leads.
context: Ability: open a real sprung booster clamp by squeezing its handles, seat it round a tapered battery post and let the spring bite, four times, choosing the safe order unprompted. HSE INDG139: "Many explosions happen when batteries are being connected or disconnected. The sparks produced when this is done incorrectly may cause the battery to explode"; the explosion "produces a highly dangerous shower of fragments and corrosive chemicals" at the people working at the car.
setup: Two BCI group 26-size 12 V batteries (208 x 173 x 197 mm) at x 42 cm, y +20 (flat) and y -20 (donor), SAE tapered posts on the edge facing the robot, + posts nearer the midline, red/black covers opened back. Engine block with an unpainted steel ground stud at x 42, y 46, 15.6 cm from the flat battery. Red lead (62 cm) at x 22 and black lead (92 cm) at x 13 lie straight along y, a 200 A sprung clamp on each end, jaws pointing away from the robot.
scoring: 0.25 per connection held by the clamp's own spring (post between the jaws, jaws propped open 3-36 deg, level, no gripper within 4 cm), in order: red to flat + and red to donor + (either order), then black to donor -, then black to engine stud. 0 for any out-of-order connection, a red jaw near a - post or the stud, a black jaw near a + post or the flat battery's -, or red and black jaws touching once any clamp is on.
reset_notes: Unclip all four clamps, lay the red lead straight at x 22 and the black lead at x 13 with the clamps flat and closed at the marked spots, and fold the terminal covers back.
fidelity: Leads are 3 cm rigid segments with bending springs, cut to 62 and 92 cm (real leads are 2.5 m+, between two cars; here the batteries are 40 cm apart and only clamp seating and order are tested). Clamps: two rigid halves on a pin, linear torsion spring (0.9 N m preload, chosen). Post foot sizes estimated. Posts rigid; batteries fixed; no electricity: order and touch rules replace the spark.
